title: NTAG213 NFC Stickers — 144-Byte Entry-Tier NFC Type 2 Tag for URL + Review + Marketing
summary: This NFC Forum Type 2 Tag chip is the most widely deployed NFC tag in the world — a 13.56 MHz passive sticker with 144 bytes of user memory, NFC Forum Type 2 Tag certification per ISO/IEC 14443-3 Type A, and native compatibility with iPhone 7+ and every NFC Android phone. The entry-tier chip-family-anchor for URL redirects, Google review links, social-media landing pages, vCard shortlinks, NFC marketing campaigns and any application where memory demand is modest and per-unit cost matters. Available wholesale in rolls (500 / 1,000 / 5,000 per roll), sheets and custom sizes Ø18-50 mm with optional NDEF pre-encoding, UID-CSV manifest and CMYK custom print.
heroPoints: Compatible with every NFC-enabled smartphone (iPhone 7 and later, all NFC Android phones) — no app required.

sections.title: Common problems buyers face when sourcing NTAG213 NFC stickers

items.label: User memory — ~132 char URL after NDEF overhead
Native iOS NFC tap (iOS 14+ background NDEF)
Native browser URL launch on tap
Lowest barrier to entry across NTAG family

bullets: Pre-encoded URL too long for 144-byte memory. A buyer ordering NTAG213 stickers pre-encoded with a full Google review URL discovers their URL (190 characters) exceeds the 132-character NDEF capacity of NTAG213, requiring either a URL shortener or an upgrade to NTAG215.

Sticker adhesive fails on textured or curved surfaces. A restaurant supply company applying NTAG213 stickers to the underside of tables (curved laminate) finds stickers peeling within 2 weeks due to poor adhesive-to-substrate bond on the textured surface.

Inconsistent read range across different phones. A retailer deploying NFC shelf labels finds that some customers' Android phones cannot reliably read a small Ø18 mm NTAG213 at the expected tap distance, while the same tag reads fine on iPhone; the root cause is the small antenna area vs older Android NFC reader sensitivity.

No UID log provided. A marketing agency deploying 20,000 uniquely tracked NFC stickers needs a UID-to-location mapping to correlate tap analytics with physical placement; suppliers without a UID log require manual scan of every sticker.

Substrate colour bleeds through transparent sticker. Buyers ordering transparent NTAG213 stickers to apply on coloured product packaging find the antenna pattern is clearly visible through the clear film, creating an unintended visual element that the brand has not approved.

sections.title: Per-tap data published from a Proud Tek NTAG213 NFC sticker

dataHighlight.heading: Maximum NDEF URL length within NTAG213 144-byte user memory
dataHighlight.text: NTAG213 user memory is 144 bytes (36 pages × 4 bytes); NDEF URI Record overhead is 7-10 bytes, leaving approximately 132-137 characters of URL capacity. Most Google Business Profile review shortlinks (g.page/r/...) are well under 80 characters; bit.ly and similar URL shorteners are under 30 characters. Custom branded shortlinks should be tested for byte count before ordering — UTM-tagged URLs commonly exceed 130 characters with tracking parameters and require NTAG215 (504 bytes) or NTAG216 (888 bytes) upgrade.
dataHighlight.source: NXP NTAG213/215/216 datasheet (NT2H1311G0DU); NFC Forum Type 2 Tag Operation Specification + NDEF URI Record Type Definition (RTD).

bullets: URL NDEF: 7-10 byte overhead + URI scheme byte + URL chars — total ≤144 byte memory.
Static URL: identical bytes on every tap — counterfeiter-clonable (no cryptographic anti-counterfeit).
32-bit PWD_AUTH password: prevents unauthorised re-write but does NOT prevent UID/URL clone.
7-byte UID: factory-burned, unique, readable — basis for analytics + UID-mapped backend.
OTP irreversible lock: permanent read-only state — appropriate for finalised deployments.

sections.title: NTAG213 timeline — from NFC Forum founding to ubiquitous consumer NFC

items.label: 2001 — NFC Forum founded
items.text: NXP, Sony and Nokia found the NFC Forum to standardise short-range (13.56 MHz) tag-based interaction; ISO/IEC 14443-3 Type A becomes the dominant transmission protocol for NFC tag chips.

items.label: 2007 — NTAG203 introduces 144-byte tier
items.text: NXP NTAG203 establishes the 144-byte user-memory + Type 2 Tag Operation Specification format that becomes the basis for the entire NTAG21x family.

items.label: 2013 — NTAG213/215/216 family launches
items.text: NXP refreshes the NTAG203 line with NTAG213/215/216 — same Type 2 Tag T2T format, but with PWD_AUTH password protection, faster command set and tighter memory tiering (144/504/888 bytes).

items.label: 2014 — iPhone 6 + Apple Pay normalises NFC handsets
items.text: Apple ships iPhone 6 with NFC for Apple Pay only; combined with widespread Android NFC, every consumer smartphone now ships with native NFC reading capability for the first time.

items.label: 2018 — iOS 12 background NFC enables URL launch
items.text: Apple iOS 12 enables background NDEF reading on iPhone XS / XR — tap-tag-to-URL works without an app for the first time on iPhone. NTAG213 becomes the default tag of choice for Google review NFC stickers, marketing campaigns, vCard tap, social-media tap and consumer-NFC at scale.

items.label: 2019-2021 — NFC marketing + Google review explosion
items.text: NTAG213 NFC stickers become ubiquitous in restaurants, hotels, clinics, retail and direct-mail marketing — replacing QR codes for tap-to-URL flows where consumer engagement rate uplift over QR is documented at 4-5x.

items.label: 2022-2024 — NFC ESL + smart-poster + table-stand verticals
items.text: NTAG213 expansion into electronic shelf labels (ESL companion), smart-poster out-of-home advertising and NFC restaurant table-stands. Larger antenna sizes (Ø25-38 mm) become standard for shelf-edge placement to ensure cross-phone read consistency.

items.label: 2026 — Today: NTAG213 chip-family-anchor for entry-tier NFC
items.text: Operating-playbook notes for google-review-restaurant, hotel-room-amenity, marketing-poster-campaign, vcard-trade-show-badge and smart-home-automation programmes converge on NTAG213 as the default entry-tier NFC sticker — with NTAG215 (504 B) and NTAG216 (888 B) reserved for memory-bound applications and NTAG 424 DNA reserved for cryptographic anti-counterfeit deployments.

faq.question: How long is the URL I can store on NTAG213?
faq.answer: NTAG213 has 144 bytes of user memory. A URL NDEF record uses 7-10 bytes of overhead, leaving approximately 132-137 characters for the URL itself. Most standard short URLs (bit.ly, Google shortened review links) fit easily. If your URL exceeds this length, use NTAG215 (504 bytes) or NTAG216 (888 bytes).

faq.question: Does NTAG213 work with all iPhones?
faq.answer: NTAG213 works with iPhone 7 and later (all models from 7 to the current iPhone lineup). iPhone 6 and earlier do not have NFC tap-to-read capability. On iPhones, the native NFC reading (no app required) has been available since iOS 14 for all NDEF-formatted NFC Forum Type 2 tags including NTAG213.

faq.question: Can I lock the sticker so the URL cannot be changed?
faq.answer: Yes. NTAG213 supports a 32-bit password (PWD_AUTH) that can be configured to protect the memory from writes. You can also use the one-time programmable (OTP) lock bits to permanently lock specific memory pages. This is irreversible, so the URL becomes read-only forever. For most URL applications, write protection (password-only) is preferred over permanent lock.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity?
faq.answer: 100 stickers for standard sizes (Ø18, Ø22, Ø25, Ø30, Ø38 mm) in white PET without custom printing. Custom-printed stickers start at 500 pieces. For pre-encoded stickers (URL written before shipment), minimum is also 100 pieces. Contact us for samples.

faq.question: Can NTAG213 stickers be used outdoors?
faq.answer: Standard white PET NTAG213 stickers are rated for indoor use. For outdoor applications, we recommend adding an epoxy dome (for maximum durability) or a UV-protective laminate. The NFC chip itself operates from −25 °C to +70 °C, but the adhesive and face stock must be specified for outdoor conditions. Ask about our outdoor-rated NFC sticker options.
